name: Coriander
grown_as: An annual herb sown for its leaves (cilantro) and seed. Leaf varieties such as 'Calypso' or 'Leisure' are slow to bolt; all look alike.
habit: At first a low leafy tuft 15 to 25 cm high; when it bolts a slender branched stem 40 to 60 cm, its leaves becoming finer as it rises. Stem smooth, solid, often flushed red-purple at the base. The leaves have the familiar strong coriander smell.

leaf.arrangement: Lower leaves in a loose rosette; stem leaves alternate
leaf.type: Two kinds. Lower leaves once pinnate with 3 to 7 broad leaflets, or simply three-lobed. Upper stem leaves two or three times pinnate, cut into narrow thread-like segments.
leaf.leaflets: On lower leaves: fan-shaped to round, 1 to 3 cm, the end leaflet largest and often three-lobed
leaf.outline: Lower leaves broad and flat, like flat-leaved parsley but softer and rounder; upper leaves feathery
leaf.base: Lower leaflets wedge-shaped at the base
leaf.margin: Lower leaflets with blunt rounded lobes and teeth all round the outer edge, none at the narrow base
leaf.surface: Thin, smooth, hairless, a little glossy
leaf.stalk: Lower leaves on long thin stalks with a narrow sheath at the base

flower.form: Small loose umbels with a ragged edge, because the outer flowers have their outer petals much enlarged
flower.petals: Five per flower; in the outer flowers the outward-facing petals are 3 to 4 times larger and two-lobed, the inner ones tiny
flower.colour: White or pale pink to mauve
flower.centre: Tiny pale stamens and a pale stylopodium
flower.behind: No bracts or one; a few narrow bracteoles under each small umbel
flower.carried: At the ends of stems and branches on longish stalks, facing up; 2 to 5 rays only, so the umbel is small and open
flower.size: Umbels 1.5 to 3 cm across; outer flowers about 3 to 5 mm
flower.season: June to August, earlier when it bolts in heat

fruit: Hard round balls 3 to 5 mm across, two halves joined, with fine wavy ribs and a tiny crown of sepals at the top. Green, ripening straw-brown. Sold as coriander seed.
seedling: Two long, narrow, strap-shaped seed leaves (about 2 to 3 cm), then first true leaves round to fan-shaped, lobed and toothed

leaf: a lower leaf with broad fan-shaped lobed leaflets
blunt teeth round the outer edge, none at the wedge base
bloom: outer flowers with much larger outer petals, giving a ragged edge
seed: round hard ball with fine ribs
seedling: first true leaf rounded and lobed
young: low tuft of broad lobed leaves on thin stalks
crop: leafy tuft of broad lobed leaves, no flower stem
flower: slender branched stem with fine feathery upper leaves
small white or pale pink umbels with enlarged outer petals
seedhead: clusters of round straw-brown seeds on few rays

look_alikes: Flat-leaved parsley has firmer, darker, glossier leaflets with sharp teeth and never thread-like upper leaves. Chervil leaves are fern-like and soft. Anise lower leaves are similar but the plant is downy and its fruit egg-shaped.
